open: In the name of Allah. Assalamu alaikum, my dears. Come closer, tonight’s story is very beautiful.
s1a: Noah… Ilyas… Have you ever been really sick? With a high fever, and you had to stay in bed for days?
s1b: Yes! It was sooo boring. And my throat hurt so much!
s1c: Oh, my dear. Get warm and cosy… Today I’ll tell you about a prophet who became very sick, and he was patient: the Prophet Ayyub, peace be upon him.
s2a: Ayyub had a family he loved, and he worshipped Allah sincerely. Then came a great test: adversity touched him, and he became very sick, very sick indeed.
s2b: Very sick? Why does Allah let a prophet be so sick?
s2c: That is a very good question, my dear. Our Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked: Which people are tested most severely? He said: The prophets, then the best, and then the next best. A test means a trial. And he said: The greatness of the reward comes with the greatness of the trial, and when Allah loves a people, He tests them. Whoever is content will have Allah’s pleasure, and whoever is angry will have His anger. And he told us that no tiredness, no illness, no worry and no sadness befalls a Muslim, not even a thorn that pricks him, without Allah wiping away some of his sins through it.
s3a: When someone is sick, they are very happy when someone visits them and asks how they are.
s3b: I like it when someone visits me when I’m sick!
s3c: That’s right, my dear. That is why we should visit the sick. Our Prophet told us that Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection: O son of Adam, I was sick and you did not visit Me. He will say: O my Lord, how could I visit You, when You are the Lord of the worlds? Allah will say: Did you not know that My servant so-and-so was sick and you did not visit him? Did you not know that if you had visited him, you would have found Me with him?
s3d: And Ayyub? Did he never complain?
s3e: Ayyub stayed patient. And Allah praised him in the Qur’an: He said that He found him patient, an excellent servant, and one who always turns back to Allah. And Ayyub called on his Lord with a very beautiful prayer.
s4a: Allah says: “And [mention] Job, when he called to his Lord, ‘Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.’” Did you hear? He told his Lord what had happened to him, and he mentioned Allah’s mercy.
s4b: That’s a beautiful dua! Can I say it too when I’m sick?
s4c: Of course, my dear! It is a prayer from the Qur’an. Everyone may say it.
s5a: Allah said to him: “Strike the ground with your foot; this is a spring for a cool bath and drink.” That means: stamp on the ground with your foot! Here is cool water to wash with and to drink.
s5b: And Allah says: “So We responded to him and removed what afflicted him of adversity. And We gave him back his family and the like thereof with them as mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers.” That means: Allah took the adversity away from him, and gave him his family and the like of them with them.
s6a: And our Prophet Muhammad told us another beautiful thing about Ayyub: while Ayyub was washing, locusts of gold fell on him, all made of gold! And Ayyub began scooping them with his hands into his garment.
s6c: Then his Lord called him: O Ayyub, have I not made you rich enough to need nothing of what you see? Ayyub said: Yes indeed, by Your might, my Lord! But I can never do without Your blessing.
s7a: Oh… they’ve fallen asleep. My dears… when you are sick or tired, be patient like Ayyub. Say his beautiful prayer: My Lord, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful. Visit people who are sick. And when you are healthy, say: Alhamdulillah.
s7b: And next time, I’ll tell you about Shuaib… and about people who cheated with measure and weight. And you, watching us right now: if you liked the story, ask your parents to subscribe to our channel, so you don’t miss the next story.
close: And you, dear fathers and mothers: subscribe to our channel, and share these stories with the people you love, so that together we pass on the beautiful message of Islam to our children.
final: Good night, my dears. I entrust you to Allah, with whom nothing entrusted is ever lost.
